utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than one. Maybe less than four. Three. Between one and three barricades. I cannot tell you the exact number. We -- you couldn't actually see how many of them there were. They were just removed to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Later when you were working at the MUP in Vukovar, did you receive information as to the locations of the barricades they put up across town?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you were at this position on the -- for 24 days was any of your tanks destroyed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that there was a tank of yours that was destroyed in that period?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be certain. I know that one captain was wounded and another soldier was wounded, two bullets in his knee. I know that. But I don't know about tanks or APCs. Maybe later after I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were in Vukovar, you said, for two months?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A bit less.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have information as to how many JNA tanks had been destroyed in that time since you were in the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that there are witnesses who were part of Croatian armed forces and there is written documentation that I will not name from which we see that over 300 JNA tanks were destroyed in that period, do you have a comment? Do you allow the possibility that it's true?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot talk about things I don't know. I don't know if a tank was destroyed, whether there were more or less of them destroyed. But the figure is not familiar, 300 tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you think less were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything. I can't tell you whether there were more or less. I didn't even know that there were any tanks destroyed, or the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we have to clear up one matter concerning prisoners of war and we'll be able to do that quickly if you look at your statement from which I will read. So you stated today that those three prisoners with that rifle called Rumunjka were walking towards active duty troops, they were bitten a lot by mosquitos, and they were later killed in the way you described?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now please take the statement you gave to the OTP, so not the one that you're holding now, but another one. B/C/S version page 3, paragraph 3, English version page 3, paragraph 4. I will read it out, and you will just follow. "On the 14th of May -- on the 14th of September, Seselj's men went to the peripheral settlement of Luzac and we followed immediately after them to clear the area after they put it under their control. When I arrived, I saw that three civilians had surrendered to reservists - I emphasise reservists - who had bound their feet and hands, left them in the cornfield, and then left to inform the army they had captured them. "The next day one lieutenant from Knin, whose name I don't know, told us to go and fetch all the three of them, and when we arrived there we saw that they were badly swollen from mosquito bites and starved, so we took them to the staff in Negoslavci. Later I heard from the Croatian police that all the three of them had been killed, one of them having been crucified on a train carriage and shot at with a tank shell."

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true this part that we went -- they came into the settlement of Luzac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Is it true that this is written in your statement?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not quite like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that OTP investigators did not take your statement accurately?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the interpreter did not interpret it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I want to have a decent discussion with you, sir. This is a large text mentioning all sorts of units. It says the next day you went to fetch those prisoners captured by reservists. Are you denying now all that is written in the statement? Are you denying, refuting this part?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They must have misinterpreted it, the interpreters, I mean. I said about those three civilians, that they had surrendered to the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I prefer to question you, if you don't mind. Let's take another statement, because this one is incorrect. That statement was, in fact, your testimony in the Ovcara case in Belgrade on the 26th of October, 2004. B/C/S version page 37, English page 38, line 45 onwards. So please find page 37 and try to follow. In the OTP statement we have the date of 14th September. Now here it says: "On the 17th of September, some civilians surrendered themselves. They were walking towards us, active duty troops. Three of them. They were dressed in civilian clothes. One of them had this Kalashnikov rifle, Romanian, I think they called it. And they came to us. The captain who was our commander asked them, 'Where are you heading?' And they answered, 'We're running away from the town because almost the entire town is on fire.' One could see a cloud of smoke, and they said, 'We're running away because we're afraid.' And so they took this rifle away from them, they bound their hands, and tied them to a tree lest they ran away from us. They were badly bitten by mosquitos overnight, so they had stains on their faces. And they drove them away, put them in a transporter, this combat vehicle is called a transporter, military transporter, and they were driven away in the direction of Negoslavci so that I have no idea, no clue, nor have I heard any more about those civilians. They simply disappeared." Is that the statement you gave in the Ovcara trial?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Will you please stop? Next question. This is the statement you gave in 2004 in which it says you have no clue what happened to those prisoners. Just a minute. You also said that this is your statement, and you stand by it. All the rest -- I don't know what you want to say.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to tell you that while I was a JNA soldier I didn't know what was going on with those civilians and what they did to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You didn't know in 2004?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't know what?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll finish with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement given in 2004 not even then did you know what happened to those civilians?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was a JNA soldier. At that time I didn't know. When I came to the police, I explained about that group, described where they were going. It may be that those were another three civilians, but they told me that the three civilians were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that before the Court where you testified under oath to this very important fact? Instead you said very decisively in 2004: "I don't know, I have no clue, nor have I ever heard any more about those people. They simply vanished." Isn't that what you said? Were you not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was telling the truth. Please don't tell me any different.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Next question. This event, did it happen on the 14th of September or the 17th?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said between the 14th and the 16th, or the 14th and the 17th. I don't see what these questions have to do with Ovcara and the massacre that was perpetrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please do not try to find a way out. We'll discuss that later. I'm asking you whether it was the 14th or the 17th, and your answer is?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 14th or the 17th, whether it was the 15th or the 16th or maybe even the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you were talking to the crime investigation police in Bjelovar in 1994 [realtime transcript read in error "2004"], so the police, you were asked on page 3, paragraph 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's an error in the transcript. It says Bjelovar 2004. We said 1994. Thank you for that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned dates like the 14th of September and the 17th September. At no point, speaking to the crime investigation police, did you mention those captives, those prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know whether the police shared all this information with you. I -- they questioned me for two days. I can't believe that all I said in two days is recorded here. Maybe you didn't receive all the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Dear Mr. Dodaj, are you seeing now before you the statement you gave to the crime investigation police in Bjelovar?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the part of the captives is missing?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you give another statement to the crime investigation police in Bjelovar that we don't know about?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: While you were a policeman in Vukovar, did you notice that there were snipers at your positions?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. At least not where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any snipers on the water-tower?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So we come to Vukovar. You surrendered, spent three days in detention; is that so?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We won't go on about that. You also said you saw three JNA soldiers taken prisoner. You spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hospital. They were undergoing treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: On your way from the JNA to the police in Vukovar, what was that road and which populated areas did you go through? So it is a fortified position of the JNA that you are starting from. Which path did you take?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was close to this hunter's lodge, and we came up to a civilian person. We asked him to go ahead and tell people not to shoot at us, and so he went. He probably said that there were five soldiers behind him who want to surrender. We surrendered to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. You said five soldiers.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please describe the road you crossed from the hunter's lodge to the police station.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you. As we were lined up that was our position and so we went in the middle of the day. I think it was noon or 2.00 p.m. We were in front of the soldiers. We went to those houses. Nobody was in those houses, they were empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We heard that.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the place is called where I crossed. I don't know where I got there. I mean, I know those people. I know that they were civilians who were living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the civilians who were living in that house. I'm asking you about the path you took to the MUP and you say you don't know. Thank you. So let's move on. Could we please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what the witness said. They were overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at Exhibit 156 on the screen? We don't have that on the screen. All right. Can we zoom in to the centre a little bit, please? Could we zoom in a little more, please? I would like to ask you to zoom in the map a little more towards the middle. Could we zoom in a little more, please? This is too much; perhaps we can pull back a notch. Thank you. This is good.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Question for the witness: Can you indicate here where the MUP was?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Could you mark the place where you think the MUP was situated with a cross?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was around here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you place a number 1 to the right of the cross and put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just place a number 1 next to it because you've already caused a confusion. Not there.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we erase this, perhaps? Perhaps we could erase it and I could start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, just put a number 1 outside of the circle. Place a cross.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. To the right of the cross, can you write down number 1 and then you can circle the whole thing now.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you please indicate where your positions were, the Sunce that you mentioned in response to my colleague's question?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Cross, place a cross, and then one centimetre to the right you can put a number 2 there and circle it.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a circle around the number 2, just the number 2. It's very simple. Can you indicate where the positions were of Hrkic and Ravlija. You talked about that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't say that. You obviously didn't listen to what I said. Hrkic, Samir and Srecko, Ravlija were at the police cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right, all right. Hrkic, Samir was not in any position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to save this on the screen, perhaps it can be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 237, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like the witness to find the statement it gave to the police in Bjelovar in the -- dated the 1st of February, 1994. B/C/S page 2, paragraph 7; English version page 3, paragraph number 5. I'm going to read and you can follow it. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm reading your statement which you found [as interpreted] in Bjelovar. "After being checked, I joined the MUP units." This is page 3, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot find this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you find a statement that you gave to the criminal police in Bjelovar?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Find page 3. So the last paragraph, it states very nicely at the bottom, number 3, and it begins, "After the check." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After the check"...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You're looking at page 2. Please look at page 3. Have you found it? The last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, here it is. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are we looking at page 3, the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the vetting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm reading now. "After the vetting, I -- he joined the MUP units in Vukovar, and was deployed on positions or rather the region called Sunce towards the Danube. Zlogledja, Zlatko and Dohanaj, Lorenc were deployed on positions in the direction of Luzac. Hrkic and Ravlija were not deployed, and they were mostly moving around the MUP building." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These first two mentioned, Zlogledja and Dohanaj, can you tell us where are these positions towards Luzac that they took up as members of the MUP? Can you indicate this on the map and can you mark it? Take the marker.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, before the witness indicates the position, these other two were not mentioned, Hrkic, Samir and Ravlija, Srecko who were said to be moving around, mostly around the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they crossed over to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So this is what it states here, but it was not recorded in the transcript. Thank you. Can you indicate the positions for which you yourself said were the positions where they were deployed, positions towards Luzac?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toward Luzac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luzac is here. I will circle it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where were the positions where they were?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were at Luzac, in Luzac, in front Luzac, behind Luzac, I don't know. I know that they were somewhere in the area of Luzac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was this, what was the month, which period was it?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: October?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you come to your positions?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which positions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This one, the Sunce position?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At about that same time in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Early October?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not early October. Perhaps mid-October. I think it was October. I know it was October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long were you at that position?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were there until we received an order to withdraw and that the town had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many of you were there at that position?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About eight, ten, I don't know. You could say that there were about eight of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were all armed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we all had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You all had police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had grey police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you were in these uniforms right until the fall?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not until the fall. I wasn't in uniform until the fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. You said that you were at the positions until the end. Where you constantly in uniform, in the MUP uniform? Were you in the MUP uniform constantly while you were at the position?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were the other MUP members also in uniforms, or as members of the Croatian MUP, were you wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people who were in uniform right until the end. There were people who were in civilian clothes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When later?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please don't ask me to give you the dates. I told you that I joined the MUP ranks voluntarily. Nobody forced me to do that. I had weapons -- or I had a weapon until I went to the hospital. On entering the hospital I threw away my weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And the uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the uniform. I told you I threw away my uniform after 20 days and after that I was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain, and you said earlier that members of the MUP were regular Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How could they be members of the regular units as you described them and be wearing different clothing and uniforms, civilian clothes? You really must explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the Croatian MUP and the ZNG had nobody to issue them uniforms and weapons, for example, as the Chetniks did. The army issued them with weapons and uniforms as well as the reservists. They had nobody to get uniforms from. There was civilians wearing civilian clothes who were defending the town. You cannot spend a month wearing the same clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the first time that you received the MUP uniform and was it new?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't packed. It was a clean uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking, was it new?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was does it mean, was it new?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you should know that.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could say that, it was new, yes. You could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why are you evading an answer?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not evading. It was not packed in a bag. I just received it like this, and it said "police" on it milicija."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What was the kind of cap that you had?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a grey beret. That was the working uniform of the MUP at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what was the insignia on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Croatian coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And the others, did they receive new police uniforms when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who arrived, Lorenc and Zlogledja, Zlatko, they received uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: New police uniforms --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And when your uniform got dirty, when didn't you ask for a new one?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the MUP burnt down, the whole MUP down, I told you the whole MUP building burned down. Only the walls remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you say that you only wore the uniform for 20 days.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wore it for a month or 20 days. I mean, really, I couldn't tell you exactly how many days. But I did wear it for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the defence line is not that you are denying it, but just when and where you removed the uniform, this is important here, so please don't interrupt and answer however you want, but we really need to move along gradually.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that after 20 days you took the uniform off and put on civilian clothes. Does that mean that for the rest of the month you were wearing civilian clothes but you were still a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. I mean, you could say that I wore uniform for more of the time than I wore civilian clothes. Whatever you think. I mean, you can take it however you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you need to tell me that yourself.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can take it that I wore uniform for more time than I wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a month, less than a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. You said that you could not get new uniforms because the MUP had burned down to the ground. And in response to my colleague's question you said that this was about 10 days before you were told that Vukovar had fell?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 10 to 15 days. It could be two weeks, it could be less than two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But it could not be less than a week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it couldn't be less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that that was when you released the captured civilians, two or three weeks before that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not three weeks before that. I don't know the dates. I just know that they were released. They even broke down the door because the man who had the key was killed, so they had to break down the door so that those people wouldn't burn down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Does that mean, as you said, only the foundations remained, that it was all destroyed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the building is still there in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that after seven days, or seven days before you entered the hospital six, five, four, three, two, one, and let's count backwards, it wasn't burning anymore, it had been hit 10 or 15 days before that, so you rule out the possibility that it could have been hit two or three days before the day you went to the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us about this elderly woman and her husband? Did you keep them there as hostages?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they were keeping them, but since they were detained, they were captured. I don't know if they were being held as hostages, but that day they were released as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you that. Did you have telephone contacts with the barracks since you said that the captain was in the barracks and he was the son of these two elderly people?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the police. That that lady, the mother, had a son who was a JNA captain in the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the reason why they were taken captive and why they were held as hostages, so that the captain would surrender? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did they talk with the barracks by telephone then?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about Jastreb younger and older?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of both of them, especially Jastreb Mladi, the younger one. I knew him. When I returned from the prison in Serbia, I met him two or three months before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk about this testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the testimony today? No, I didn't know that I would come. I wasn't sure that I would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Who is the Jastreb that you met at the time of the Vukovar operations?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you anything that I don't know. I heard from what he said that he was the commander of the Vukovar defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stipe Pole. He was the chief of the police in Vukovar. His name was Stipe Pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And the -- you from the MUP of Croatia positions and the Sunce positions on the Danube, were you able to see Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I was at Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I escaped from the JNA, 10 days after that I went to see Mitnica. I was interested in seeing what it looked like. It was completely demolished. Not a single house was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And when was this, in which period?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in early October, beginning of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is something new. So tell us more about it. Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took a MUP vehicle. Myself and another boy who trained boxing. He later got killed, unfortunately. I didn't spend a long time there. I just went to see how badly it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you find any ZNG positions, Home Guards positions in Mitnica, and do you know that the Home Guard Corps had its positions at Mitnica while you were there?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know where the fair-grounds were?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe I passed by, but I didn't know it was the fair-ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As a member of the MUP, did you know that Home Guards had their positions there at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They must have had.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about ZNG positions in Luzac?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were probably there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you hear about Bogdanovci? Was there a larger ZNG unit there?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that while I was a JNA soldier, Lorenc Dohanaj saw his uncle through the binoculars somewhere near Bogdanovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: His uncle was in ZNG positions?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Croatian army. It was a recognised army of Croatia. I don't know why you're questioning me about that. If there were paramilitaries units, as we know there were, why don't you ask me about the paramilitaries and volunteers and all the others who were coming in from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Am I being questioned now?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on. Since you were a MUP member, to the best of your knowledge there were some ZNG members who came to fetch food on the premises of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have been at Mitnica, Luzac, anywhere else. They were defending their own town, Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you say "everywhere," where is that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the direction of Luzac, Mitnica. I was close to Sunce. I don't know if there were any other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the Danube Hotel, Dunav Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like another missing piece of the answer to be recorded. And the witness said there were positions in Borovo settlement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said "probably."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who occupied the high school building during those operations, members of the ZNG or MUP?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was captured by who? Occupied by who?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Whether ZNG or MUP.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would they occupy a building in their own town?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: During the Vukovar combat was there any -- anyone in those positions?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that after two months spent in Vukovar you pulled back to the area around the hospital; is that correct? In your statement to the OTP, page 4, paragraph 2; English version page 4, paragraph 2, you said you had withdrawn to the area around the hospital.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We withdrew closer to the hospital, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where were you in the area around the hospital, could you tell us a bit closer, before you entered into the hospital? Please be so kind and calm down and answer my questions slowly. So what were the positions around the hospital to which you withdrew, as you said in your statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day Vukovar fell we all withdrew to a basement. It was a building; I can't tell which. There were also many civilians there. And when the chief, Stipe Pole, and another couple of policemen, I don't know the exact number, if there were 30 or more than 30, they formed a group that got out of Vukovar. That's where we were, in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'll be asking you more about this. So you said you withdrew, according to establishment, to some basement. How far from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you how many metres away from the hospital, maybe 500, maybe 20 metres. I don't know. It was a building with a large basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, there is a big difference between 20 metres and 500.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the building or what this place was called, where the basement was. You are not letting me tell you what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you about what happened later, but for now I want yes or no answers.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just explain what was located in that basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I just asked you how far it was from the hospital. You told me 500 or 20.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you don't know, never mind. Let's move on. How many of you policemen were there?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 50 or 60. 50 to 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you all armed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were all armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it your combat position or police position that had not yet fallen by that time?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just withdrew there in order to be able to get out of Vukovar. There were no positions of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why then did you then mix with the civilians, carrying weapons, 50 or 60 of you?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Why did we mix with the civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you because Vukovar had not fallen yet.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a question of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You said you attempted to break the enemy lines after that?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not break through the enemy lines. Our chief, Stipe Pole, managed somehow to get out of Vukovar. What kind of break-through do you think that was with the huge amount of weapons at the disposal of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement given in the Ovcara trial in Belgrade, page 38, 39 in English, we are still on line 48, you are talking about the break-through.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If you want, let's call it break-through. But it wasn't really a break-through. If you insist, though, let's call it break-through. What kind of break-through is that if nobody fired a bullet?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you were all armed?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. I'm not saying we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When one exits a building in circumstances where the enemy side is also there, around, does that mean in military terms that you were breaking through, in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military break-through, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So what do you call it, a civilian break-through?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let it be your way. Let it be a military break-through.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So how many were you in that group?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three groups were formed. I told you the chief, Stipe Pole, with his policemen, who were mainly middle-aged men, got out of Vukovar. I was in the second group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lorenc, Kuscevic, Petar, Hrkic, Samir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 or 30 or 60, I don't know. I can't tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. You tell me there were 30 or 60 in your second group?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you attempted a break-through and then at some point you gave up?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to tell you how it was. Stipe Pole, in fact, one man said, "Dear gentlemen, each group will have a guide. You don't need to be afraid. The delay, the interval between groups will be half an hour." However, when the first group left we reached the Vuka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's enough of an answer.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me go on. A man was supposed to wait for us near a ranger's lodge, but nobody was waiting. We were supposed to take a boat. Two men managed to cross over the canal, and my friend Lorenc Dohanaj ran after them and stepped on an anti-personnel grenade, anti-personnel mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How far away was it from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I know that I crossed over the cemetery and the pitch in Vukovar. How far from the hospital that was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: From the Vuka River, going back, you were all armed again, right?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question was were you all armed.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about myself. I don't know about anything else. I know about Zlatko Zlogledja and Hrkic, Samir, I know they were armed. I don't know about the rest because it was pitch-dark. In fact, Hrkic, Samir had a pistol, not a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you were able to see that clearly?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were together that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said in your various statements that you threw away your arms at a cemetery.

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, and Zlatko did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hide it or did you just throw it away?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just threw it away. Or maybe in an open grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you reached the hospital, did you see how far the MUP building was from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact distance, but it wasn't far. It was close.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very close?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not next door, but it's a hundred or 150 metres, but I know that you can see the hospital nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever shoot from the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But we were shot at, because we didn't have mortars, we didn't have aircraft, and we were not able to return fire. I just want you to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn later about that captain of yours who got killed at the beginning? From where did mortars shoot at your positions killing one captain and one -- wounding one soldier?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You were not interested?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you reached the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The MUP building is close by?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: At that time it wasn't burning?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'll be moving on to a different subject now. You spoke about the time you spent at the barracks and how you left for Ovcara. Now tell us this: When you set out in the convoy of buses towards Ovcara would you now be so kind as to read from what you stated to the OTP, page 48 in B/C/S -- excuse me, sorry. Page 4, paragraph 6; English, page 4, paragraph 6. I don't want to confuse you. It says: "I saw that there are about five buses lined up in the street. Men were ordered to get on. I got on to the fourth bus and sat closer to the end if you look from the head of the bus. I was sitting next to a man whose name was Horvat, as far as I know. He was married, father of two from Vinkovci. There was a guard on our bus armed with an automatic rifle. The buses set out in a convoy and shortly stopped at the barracks." Is that so? That is, about the barracks. Now, please look at what you stated at the Ovcara trial in Belgrade about your trip from the barracks to Ovcara. That's page 48. The English version, page 49, lines 13, 14. Does it say here, question by the presiding judge, in response to the question of the presiding judge, you said you were in the last bus but one and you think there were six of them, "but I was in the last but one." In the fifth bus. Now, look at what you said next: It says Counsel Todorovic: You were in the fifth bus, that's how it starts. Do you want me to read it to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJDAR DODAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You will see what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. So, you were appearing at the Ovcara trial in Belgrade and you stated the following: We heard that you abide by that statement that you gave under oath. Now, Counsel Todorovic says, and I'm reading from the transcript: "You were in the fifth bus. Did those buses travel in a convoy, one behind the other?" Witness, meaning you, answers, "Yes." Counsel Todorovic: "Was there any security detail around, some other vehicles, military vehicles going either in front or behind you?"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: transporter in front." Presiding Judge: "You think there was tank at the head?"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that -- is that written?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So it means that -- that the tank was at the head of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And this transporter was right behind it?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And then the buses followed. So there was no one else, just the tank, the transporter and the buses, nobody else? You stand by that?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You also stated another time on the occasion of that testimony, and of course you didn't mention that there was a passenger vehicle in front, a jeep and so on.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I did say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, you didn't say it there. You didn't say there, but you stand by what you said?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that the prisoners at Ovcara were abused by Arkan's men, Seselj's men and the White Eagles, whereas yesterday during questioning you said that you recognised the White Eagles because they had a white ribbon tied around their arm. Is that the only mark indicating that they belonged to Seselj's White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I assumed that they were belonging to the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that some regular soldiers for that particular operation that day also wore white ribbons on their sleeve, does that change your assumption that we're talking about Seselj's and White Eagle men?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: When we came to the outskirts of Dubrava, close to Vukovar, there were people from the reserve forces there, people wearing white ribbons and they said they were White Eagles, and that's how I understood that these other people also belonged to the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, I would briefly like to deal with the machine that you saw. You responded to my colleague's question, so I'm not going to ask too many questions about that. My colleague read out to you some text about the bucket. Yesterday on page 5541, line 24, up to page 5542, line 2, you said -- this is in the corrected transcript, Your Honours. If you don't have the corrected transcript it's on page 54, lines 22 to 25. In response to a question did you see that vehicle, thinking of this machinery, you said it was a yellow bulldozer. Did you see that it went anywhere, that was the question. And you answered: "No, I didn't. I saw a soldier getting on to the machine and turning the ignition on and the machine remained on." That is your answer, and you remain by that answer. Now the question: At any point, and I don't want to confuse you, did anyone use the bucket to remove earth from one place and put it in another place while you were there?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was anybody digging a hole on the road during that time?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And how about across the street?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anybody digging?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anybody digging while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see anywhere behind the hangar that the machine was making a hole or not?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Please, sir, I'm telling you that as long as I was there, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you gave a statement to the Prosecution here, to investigators here, and on page 5, paragraph 2; English version, page 5, paragraph 3, could you please find that? I am going to read out the text, and you can follow to make sure I am reading as it is written. "We had to wait in front of the hangar while the people got out of the bus."

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what page it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The statement you gave to the Prosecution, you have page 5. Have you found it? And then at the top you have paragraph 1, and then paragraph 2. Did you find it? It starts: "From the bus." And then it says: "We had to wait" -- I'm just reading this part: "In front of the hangar while people were getting out of the bus and during that time I saw a backhoe excavator digging a hole behind the hangar." The question is: Have I read the text correctly?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Second question: Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: That I saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you if it's correct or not.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I did see an excavator, but this was not translated properly. I don't know who translated it. It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that this part of the statement that I just read out does not reflect what you stated and that this part of the statement is not correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I think that this part about digging a hole is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know, you mentioned in your statement in Bjelovar a certain Franjo, about whom you heard and you mentioned that in your statement later, that he lived in Zagreb, and that he was one of the defence commanders in Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Franjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear who the commander of the defence in Borovo Naselje was? This is your statement in -- that you gave to the criminal investigations police in Bjelovar in 1994. This is page 5, paragraph 4; English version is page 4, paragraph 6. Page 5, paragraph 4. Have you found it? So you go paragraph 1, 2, 3, 4, paragraph 4. You can read the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, I don't see exactly where it is. I don't see which page it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Page 5.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, very well. Let me. Doesn't it say that Franjo from Vukovar who is now living in Zagreb was one of the commanders of the defence in Borovo Naselje? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps the gentleman will allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. Number one, I will let you say what you want. Do you confirm that this is what it states in your statement that you gave to the police, the criminal investigations police in Bjelovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, it says that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And now go ahead and answer.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: This Franjo is not actually from Vukovar. These are people who came from Varazdin. I met him at the police administration in Vukovar, and it's possible that he was in the Borovo Naselje defence, but not that he was from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And now please tell us: Those people who came from Varazdin to the police station where you were doing the operations?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They did not come to the police station. They would come to the police station. Perhaps they happened to be at positions in Borovo Naselje, but they would go there for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did I hear you properly, ZNG members would come from positions in Varazdin?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: These were MUP members, members of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. MUP members from Varazdin would come to you, to the Vukovar MUP to get food; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How far is Varazdin from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: It's Croatia, sir. They came to their country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how far Varazdin is from -- just one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am hearing the warning from the interpreter. The witness must wait for my answer and then we will not be overlapping, but I'm not asking for your intervention. I'm almost done with my questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So since Varazdin is a town in Vukovar, you said yourself Franjo, you -- and you mentioned Varazdin. So can you please tell us how far Varazdin is from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: How far Varazdin is from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there was a mistake in the transcript that Varazdin is a town in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Varazdin is a town in Croatia. Okay. So is Varazdin a town in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Second question: At the time of the Vukovar operations, you said that members of MUP from Varazdin would come to MUP in Vukovar. How far was that town from the town of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know how many kilometres is dividing those two cities, but it's pretty far. I don't know in kilometres how far apart they are, Varazdin and Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is it over 50 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, it probably is over 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that members of the Varazdin MUP passed through all the war-stricken areas to get to your station, to take food for the MUP in Varazdin, what was the reason? Are there any other reasons for that?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't understand all the fronts. By the time I left or fled from the army, they were already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were they at the time?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They were in Borovo Naselje already.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So is your answer, or your statement that the police officers from Varazdin were in Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, they came to defend that area. They were defending the whole of Croatia. They were defending their country. It should have been an honour for them to defend their country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The policemen from Varazdin, when was the first time you saw them at the front lines in Borovo?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I never saw them there because I was not in Borovo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When did you find out that they were there. When did you find out?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: When they were coming to the MUP to get the food I would talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What period was this, what month?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I really don't know which month it was. I have no idea. It was October. Let's say that it was October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How many of the MUP members from Varazdin came to Borovo Naselje and were manning those combat positions?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Really, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did they have automatic rifles or hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Those who came had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a member of the 204th Brigade of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: What period are you thinking of now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Pick any period, just answer my question. Were you at any point a member of the 204th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: When I came home from prison, in order to secure my due rights, we were all members of the 204th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And which month was this?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: It was in 2004 when I came and that was when I requested this certificate so that I could receive the rights that were due to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you left in -- you were released in 1993?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: In 1994, early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now my last question. You spoke about Topcider yesterday, what you went through there, and you said, "I know that Topcider is close to Zemun." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is. I mean, it's close to Belgrade. It's close to Zemun. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that it is on the opposite side of Zemun, that Zemun is at one end of Belgrade and Topcider is at the opposite end from Zemun, would you change your answer?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Sir, you probably know much better than I do where Topcider is. I thought that Topcider is near Zemun.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And when you came here -- now really this is my last question. When you came here to provide a statement here to this Tribunal, did you provide any addition to your statement to the Prosecution, did you provide an additional statement and did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You didn't give an annex to your statement?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am finished with my questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. We will now have the second break and we will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dodaj, good afternoon. I am Momcilo Bulatovic, one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin. On behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Sljivancanin, I am going to be putting some questions to you, and I will try my best not to ask you questions already put by my colleagues. Maybe some things that are still a little bit unclear to this team, I would like to clarify. In order to avoid bad interpretation or wrong interpretation or something wrong going into the transcript, I would like to ask you to wait until I complete my question and then begin your answer. If you feel there is something that you need to clarify and explain, you will have enough time for that. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I did very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Before we move to actual questions, what I would like to do first is to clarify something, and I think that we will both agree about this. It's as follows: You, from 1991 until today, provided a number of statements and had a number of interviews with different institutions; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Your most recent statement was given to the department for war crimes of the special department of the district court in Belgrade in October 2004; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony from yesterday and today when you spoke about the events, you also talked about Mr. Sljivancanin, you mentioned him, so what I would like to do is to clarify some things to see if I understood them correctly. You said that you saw Mr. Sljivancanin for the first time on the 19th of November, 1991 in the afternoon; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was, but I saw him inside the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about the person who was filming, you saw him with Mrs. Bosanac, let's not repeat that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The second time you saw Mr. Sljivancanin was, you said, in the hospital on the 20th of November, 1991 in the morning; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: In the hospital and I also saw him in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how long you actually saw him, this visual contact that you had with him, how long did that last? Did you see him for a couple of seconds, a minute?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: This is what I can say. I was about two metres away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: And I did look at him for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how long that is, for quite a long time?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Until we boarded the buses. I don't know how long it was, was it half an hour, an hour, I couldn't say. But I was about two metres away from him. I was quite close to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So you were looking at him when he was in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that a staff member of the hospital told you to leave the hospital; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. We received the order that we had to leave the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You left and then what happened?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: We exited the hospital and we were lined up in front of the hospital. Before that they separated women and children to one side, and they lined us up in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After that you said, okay, that women and children left first and then after that you, and then the wounded.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, probably all the wounded came outside as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that's what you said yesterday. I don't want to confuse you.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that the wounded came out after us, immediately after us. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Then you said that on that occasion you saw representatives of international organisations who were standing next to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, they were standing to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this exit, which you used to enter and leave, so the exit where you left, how far were they from this place, from this exit?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: You mean how many metres they were away?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They were standing to the left side. I don't know how far they were standing in metres, perhaps they were 10, 15 or 20 steps away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you saw one of those representatives, you remember him because he was wearing an earring?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing an earring.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So I assume that you were not standing too far away?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I was standing some 10 to 15 steps away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about exiting the hospital, and that's something what you described yesterday, because on page 42, line 1 of the transcript it states that you said in response to a question by my learned friend from the Prosecution, you said that women and children exited first, then you and then the wounded, so I think that there is no dispute there.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. Women and children and the elderly came out. We did, everybody, then the wounded were brought out of the hospital later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how long you stayed in this line when they lined you up during this search? How long did this take?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: You mean how many hours? I don't know exactly, but it wasn't less than half an hour, it could have been longer. Only longer, I don't know whether it was an hour or a little bit less than an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After that you went to the buses; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I conclude that based on what you said earlier that Mr. Sljivancanin remained by the entrance to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After that you entered the buses. How long did you spend in the buses before you set off for the barracks?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know how long we were there, but as soon as the buses were filled, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was with you on the bus of the people that you knew?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Of those people I knew, I said it was Petar Kuscevic, Samir Hrkic, Zlatko Zlogledja, and this-- a gentleman named Horvat who was sitting next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This gentleman, Mr. Horvat, when and where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I met him at the police administration in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing at the police administration in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall at the time you spent in MUP, did he have a combat position?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about that. I met him again later at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said you saw five or six buses parked there?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I know I was in the last but one. How many there were, five or six, I don't know, but I know I was in the last but one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the buses, there were no other vehicles, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I said there were no military vehicles, and the buses were civilians and driven by civilian drivers. The civilian driver had a rifle laid next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You arrived at the barracks, the buses stopped in the way you described. And then something you already described happened. I'll skip that. There are different time indications in various statements you gave concerning your stay at the barracks. How long -- this is what I want to know. How long did the bus -- buses stay outside the barracks before they moved on to what you later learned to be Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Whether we were there for an hour, two hours, less than an hour, less than two hours, I really can't tell you. I really can't tell you anything about the number of hours we spent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In all that time that you were there, you did not see Mr. Sljivancanin at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to know about your arrival at Ovcara. Could you give us a time-frame, or at least indicate the time of day when you came to the Ovcara farm?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was. All I know was that the sun was shining very bright. How -- what time it was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your bus, the last but one, as you said, did you sit closer to the front or closer to the back?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Somewhere in the middle, perhaps closer to the back. On the right-hand side, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were your mates from the army together with you, the ones that you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me how one vacates a bus. Is it the case that one bus is emptied and then moves on, and then another moves up and is emptied? Or do they all vacate simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long does it take to empty one bus, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I can't know that. Whether it's 15 minutes or 20 minutes, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In some of your statements you mentioned that your comrade Kuscevic was the first to get off the bus.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And he was the first one to be hit?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And after that he said he was a soldier of the Yugoslav army who had been what, captured by the Croatian forces? How did the dialogue go?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I'll tell you. Before he got off one other man got off, he was wearing a cockade, and asked, "Is there anyone on this bus who is an ethnic Albanian." He could not guess that I was an ethnic Albanian just by my accent. And the man said, "If we establish that there is an ethnic Albanian among you, the whole bus will come to a bad end."
