That's when I decided to come out. When Petar Kuscevic got off the bus, somebody hit him with a shovel handle and he said, "Don't, don't hit me, I'm a JNA soldier, the Ustashas captured me." Then they helped him up on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just slow down for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: The captain was close to the bus. He pulled him too and asked, "Are there any more of you on that bus," and then he pointed, Zlatko, me, and Hrkic. And that man came up to me and said, "You were born again today." And they put us on one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I want to know were there any of you from that bus who went into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No. I never said I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking. You say that later you were separated from the others.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where did they make you stand relative to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: If we had a picture, I could show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 228. And with the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness photograph 22. It's from the 65 ter exhibits, number 228. That's the photograph, right, Mr. Dodaj?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Take this pointer, the magic pen, and please mark with a cross the place where they left you after the four or five of you were gathered, were rounded up? Where were you standing with those two colonels?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They were lieutenant-colonels.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Shall I put a cross there?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Right. I can't see it. Can you put a number 1?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: From which side?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Any side you like, as long as it's visible. And please put a circle around number 1.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you were standing there, because of the time it was taking to empty the buses one by one, was there a -- was it possible for you to see the buses, including the bus on which you were on?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No. But I could see the bus behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then please mark the position of that sixth bus. Where was it standing, the last bus? Because you were in the last but one.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, it moved away pretty quickly after we got off. It was somewhere here. It was actually closer to us. Maybe I left too much distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Never mind. Just put number 2 there, and a little circle around the number.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this exhibit as it is marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 238, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dodaj, I want to know this: Bearing in mind the photo that you marked and the whole layout, did you go on standing together with the lieutenant-colonels, were you still standing there when the last bus was emptied?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see where this last bus headed as it was leaving? Did they go back or what?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I can't tell you that, I really don't know. I don't think they went back. I can't even say whether they made a turn into the yard or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me, how long did your discussion with those two lieutenant-colonels last in the spot marked 1?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Until the hangar door closed and until the military vehicle Puch arrived with a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I want to know. How long did it take?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how much time. I can't say whether it was an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now, throughout that time while you were talking to those two lieutenant-colonels, were the five of you there together?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: You mean four?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, four.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this officer who arrived in this Puch vehicle with his driver, did you notice any other officers coming in, passing by, coming up to those lieutenant-colonels?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Apart from the officers, I saw that captain who singled out Pero Kuscevic, the two lieutenant-colonels, and the officer to came to fetch us. I didn't see any other officers. I've already said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now, about this captain, did you see what happened with this captain?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a little correction to make in the transcript. Page 87, line 22. My question was: Apart from these two lieutenant-colonels and that captain while I was standing there and talking, did he see any other officers. And the witness answered no. However, that answer is not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I said next to me there were these two lieutenant-colonels, there was one captain next to the bus and that officer who came to fetch us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you, apart from those officers, did you see any others?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I did not. But let me tell you one more thing. While we were standing outside the hangar, I know that one volunteer came and asked the lieutenant-colonel to free one of the men who were inside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You have already said that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are again speaking at the same time and later complain that things are missing from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that during your stay at Ovcara farm from the moment when you left the bus until the moment you entered the Puch vehicle which took you to Negoslavci, you did not see Mr. Sljivancanin there?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that the buses were guarded by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see those soldiers after the buses left or did they leave together with the buses as if they were escorting them?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: The soldiers came up all the way to Ovcara with us and they were the first to get off.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see what happened with them later?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I didn't see where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to tell me, if you can, to the best of your knowledge what they looked like, these two lieutenant-colonels. Please give me a description. Maybe one of my colleagues already asked you this, but please describe for me both lieutenant-colonels, that captain, and that officer who came to fetch you in any order you like. In a narrative that I will not interrupt.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They had wind-jackets, windbreakers. They were rather neat, clean. Their hair had shades of grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Two of them. I don't know their age. If somebody had asked me my name at that time, I feel I wouldn't have been able to answer. But when that man came up to them and asked them to free one man from the hangar, I was sure they occupied a high position, a senior position. They could have freed anyone they wanted. They were not particularly stout or thin. Average, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about the captain?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: The captain who came to fetch --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, you said it was an officer.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: The captain was with us. He was standing next to the bus. He had dark hair, maybe black, also a JNA uniform, rather slim.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How tall?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Between 170, 180 centimetres. I couldn't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the officer who came in the Puch vehicle?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He was also rather slim, trim, neat. He had a Heckler gun. He got out of the Puch, opened the hangar door, looked in, closed it, and left, talked for a second to the soldiers standing outside the hangar, then came up to us and told us, "Get in."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did he linger after you got into the car, talking to somebody?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. He discussed something with them, but not for long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During that time was the hangar door closed?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, it was closed. I know exactly that while the buses were emptied there were four children standing outside their door. What happened with them later, whether they were driven away and where, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to take you back to your arrival at Vukovar. Many questions have already been asked on the subject, but what's important for me is some sort of chronology that would enable me to better understand some of the things you stated here. On the 24th of September in 1991, you made the decision to leave the Yugoslav People's Army for the reasons you have already stated?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I want to know who initiated that decision? Yourself or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I -- I was. I initiated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Before you left on the 24th September, before you left the JNA in the way you've described for us, did you have any contact through anyone whatsoever with people from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: While I was on JNA positions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Before you left.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: From that place, from your position until the junction where you met some locals, as you described, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I really don't know the distance between those people and our positions. I really can't put a number. I really don't want to say any -- anything wrong again for these transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I want precisely to avoid errors on the transcript. I can ask you, for instance, was it more than five kilometres or less?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: It was less than five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said you ran into a local, a civilian, and you told him what to do and you told him that you wanted to surrender. Did you give him any instructions as to who he should inform that you wanted to surrender?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: We just asked him to tell people not to shoot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- does that mean you knew that the guardsmen were holding positions there?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I didn't know. I didn't know, how could I know? Sir, I was from Bjelovar. I telephoned from the barracks to my home and they described the situation for me. They told me there were troops, they told me there was the MUP of Croatia, they told me there was the Croatian Home Guards Corps, that's a fact. Of course there were ZNG positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And from the moment you told that civilian, that local person that you wanted to surrender to inform the guards, until the moment you reached the positions of the guard, how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He was the one who went ahead to tell the guardsmen that there were five soldiers wishing to surrender. How far, what the distance was, I really can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Once you arrived to the place where the guards were, did you speak with the members of the guard before you went to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, they asked us once we surrendered, people embraced us, one started crying, had tears rolling down his face. His brother worked in Bjelovar at a gas station, and he asked me whether I knew his brother and said the place where he was from and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who started crying?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: This member of the guards. The guards and the MUP members didn't shoot at the regular JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Nobody was wounded on our positions except for that one soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. If the guards and MUP members didn't shoot at the regular JNA soldiers, who did they shoot then?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Mostly JNA officers. This is why the officers would remove their rank insignia from their uniforms and put it in their pockets. And then if they addressed us and we would disregard them, then they would take this rank insignia from their pockets to show that they were, in fact, officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Which weapons did they use to shoot at the JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know because they didn't hit anyone except for that captain who got killed, or actually who was wounded. And that was a mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have snipers?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know that. Probably they did. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many officers of the regular JNA army died in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay with the guards members?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Not long. Because they immediately transferred us to the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If you had such friendly relations with the guards members, one of them even started crying upon hearing that you knew his brother in Bjelovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, sir, that's not what I said. He said that his brother worked in Bjelovar and he asked me whether I knew him. I told him that I wasn't from Bjelovar, but that I knew the gas station, which is in Bjelovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dodaj, first of all, I'd like to ask you not to interrupt me as I'm talking. That's number one. Number two, there is absolutely no reason for you to be so jumpy.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Third, I do my best not to put in your mouth something that you didn't say, and I always give you an opportunity to correct me if I say something wrongly. Let us now go back. Did you say that a member of the guards started crying once you got there, that they embraced you?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Listen --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, let me explain. Tears started rolling down his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You had a friendly conversation?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Naturally. Of course it was friendly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't mean anything bad when I said that. They took you to the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Since you had such friendly conversations with the guards members, why did they lock you up in the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: You could say that they put us in detention to check where we had come from and who we were and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, there are some inconsistencies here, so let's see if we can clarify? How many days did you spend in detention.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was three days, more than three days, less. I can't say that that was actually proper detention. We were together with them, watching television in the basement until -- well, we could say three days, more than three days, I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We can't seem to be able to define whether you were detained or not. You were with them together. How many of them were there, those that you were with? Were you in the same room, did you have freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: We didn't have freedom of movement until they checked who we were and where we were from and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How many days later did you ask for uniforms from the moment you arrived at the MUP?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Until they told us clearly that one couldn't leave Vukovar any longer, that it was under siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In those rooms, if I understood you well, you could watch television?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, video recorder.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So videotapes?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. We watched videotapes and we listened to Ceca sing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to watch live broadcasting?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. I watched as the powder plant was blown up in Bjelovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You said that a mother of some captain was there?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, not there, sir. Next to the police building, or rather, yes, in the detention premises of the police building. But I don't know when she arrived there and who brought her.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was she also able to watch television or do something similar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I would like now to turn to your combat assignment, positions, your positions were called Sunce, they were facing Luzac?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did other [as interpreted] have positions as well? There are some things that remained unclear to me. Because you talked about eight of you and I would like to know what happened to the other six. Let's check Lorenc first. Did he have a combat disposition?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, he was in the direction of Luzac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. What about Kobas. Did he have a combat disposition?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Hrkic?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Kuscevic?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Rasid Adzibegovic?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He didn't have it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the four of them did?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: They were in the basement of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have any kind of police or military assignments?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. They didn't even have uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So you were in the MUP building and on the positions how long -- or rather, the four of them were there until the MUP building was set on fire?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed on your positions until?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Until we were given order to pull back. It was on the 17th or 18th, I don't remember any longer, but I stayed there all the way up until we withdrew towards the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will ask you about whether you heard about the surrender of the group from Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that, but I know that Mitnica was cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You were at Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I said so. But before it had been cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you were there in October and this was the 18th of November when the Mitnica battalion surrendered?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of a person called Filip Karaula?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Not until today?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that I did hear of such a name, but I never paid attention to it. I don't know who he is and what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you --

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that he was commander of the Mitnica battalion, would that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, not to me personally. But if he was I'll take your word for it. You seem to know it. Is he still alive?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That's what he claims. That's not what I claim. Now I need to clarify something about Srecko Ravlija. He was hit by a mortar shell in the MUP yard?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know this accurately, sir. I sat there together with him, and fortunately, fortunately for me, I went to the basement right then when the shell landed and it pierced two batteries, two military batteries and severed his leg. He bled profusely and then at the hospital his leg was amputated. I don't know what date it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can we try to pin-point this in relation to the MUP building being set on fire. Did this happen before that?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, yes, before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about Adzibegovic, Rasid was he injured in an operation?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him? You were on the positions.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: He was at the police administration building in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After the MUP building was bombed do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. Rasid Adzibegovic I believe was a Montenegrin, but he was of Orthodox faith, and his brother fought on the opposite side. When Vukovar fell he went to his brother and he was -- Rasid was on very good terms with this policeman, and once this happened he took him with him, and I don't know what happened to him later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When did this happen, when did he leave Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Once the army arrived, could have been the 19th. He was with this person. I think it was on the 19th or the 20th. I think 19th. I know it was dark. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dodaj, can we agree that your recollections about these events was the freshest back in 1994 when you talked to the Bjelovar police people?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Well, in relation to the period of time, yes. One cannot remember everything at the same time. Whenever you talk about events, some new recollections emerge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. In the conversations with the inspectors or policemen from Bjelovar you spoke about three groups numbering 20 people each for break-through. You covered this with my friend Borovic, so we will not dwell on this, but I will ask you something else. After this unsuccessful break-through, if we can call it that, or unsuccessful attempt to leave Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, to leave Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, after that, go straight back to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes. We brought a man. We brought Lorenc, who had been injured by a mine, we brought him to the hospital and we stood there. We had discarded our weapons and then we entered the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On that day with Lorenc --

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Zlatko Zlogledja was there, Hrkic Samir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Please. On that day when you brought Lorenc to the hospital, once you came back, how many of you entered the hospital together with Lorenc?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say. I don't know the number. All I know is that Lorenc, myself, Hrkic and Petar Kuscevic entered the hospital together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether anybody else came in with you?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any people who entered hospital with you who wore police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know that, truly. Maybe there were such individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You turned over Lorenc to the doctors due to his injuries?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: We were in the -- on the ground floor of the hospital, or basement. I don't know what it was. Ground floor. Next to them in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember which entrance you went through when you went inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Through the same door that we went out, once we went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay at the hospital you, I mean Kuscevic, Zlogledja Hrkic and yourself, did you all stay together, or were you separate in various locations?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Mostly we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on that day, the 20th, in the morning, a meeting was held in the hospital, or something similar?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: The 20th?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know about that. We were just given an order to come out of the hospital. Whether they negotiated with Dr. Vesna Bosanac about the surrender of the hospital, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the doctors at the hospital or any civilians who had already been in the hospital, any patients or anybody else, did they tell you that the evacuation of civilians was supposed to take place from Velepromet and that Dr. Bosanac said that civilians should not come to the hospital but rather go to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I truly don't know that. All I know is that women and children were put on one side. I don't know about the rest. Maybe what you say is true, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood these events correctly, you arrived at the hospital when? On the 18th in the evening or 17th?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I think it was the 18th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I think so too. But it was the night before leaving the hospital, you spent that night at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that some lists were being drafted at the hospital for evacuation of civilians and that representatives of the Croatian Red Cross took part in drafting these lists?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You don't?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were some JNA members who were wounded and who were treated at the hospital and that there was a sergeant there and two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, I think that the sergeant was wounded. I don't know about the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew that one of them had talked to General Raseta?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: Yes, we could hear that on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to know where did you hear this on the radio, while you were at the police station, on the positions, or at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: While I was at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: "Yes, ahead of all those buses."
utterances.text: I heard them say that the army should stop shelling the hospital, the town, that the shells were landing on the hospital, that the hospital was practically all destroyed and the like. Well, those were not verbatim words, but I know that he asked that the hospital not be shelled.
